items.title: Steve "Ted" Brown Interview, 1958-04-22
items.q: He took my place when I left, when I left the band in 1913. He took my place and played from then on.

ctx.x: Well, anyway, uh, the people that stand around and listen at the band, particularly these strangers, the out-of-town people, they'd come around and, oh, they'd just holler, you know, maybe we'd hear that type of music. So, I guess it was that, uh, kind of music Tom was playing at the Yacht Club or someplace where Fishburne was dancing. And, uh, the thing that I knew was that, uh, caused Frisco to go back up to New York to tell, uh, tell the people in Lamb's Cafe about the band he heard down in New Orleans. But,…
Well, which Lai Canna was it that you mentioned, uh? Arnold Lai Canna. Arnold, huh? He went up to, with Tom.

Oh, I see. He took my place when I left, when I left the band in 1913. He took my place and played from then on. Uh, played in Chicago and went to New York with them. And, uh, the going got pretty rough in New York, I understand, for Tom and them. And, uh, Lai Canna and Lambert and Shields, I think, beat it out of New York. One other question. What did you call that band down here? What was the name of it? Well, we, uh, we called it just Brown's Band. Brown's Band. And sometimes some people would put across on…
